definition.description: From either a defined fully prone position or the bottom of one controlled push-up, the athlete pushes the floor away, recovers one chosen foot beneath the body, clears the hands, projects forward, accelerates through a prescribed short target, and uses a planned run-out. The exact variant fixes the chest/contact state. This is not a push-up set, burpee, reaction test, cone drill, or a static standing sprint.

environment.surface: clean dry non-slip non-abrasive floor start zone and clear short lane
environment.space: one protected start zone, target lane, and planned run-out
inspection: hands clear of debris and moisture
defined chest/contact state and lead-foot recovery
lane, target, footwear, run-out, and coach sightline
environment.changeRule: Changing ground contact state, hand position, cue, lead foot, distance, surface, target, run-out, rest, or intent requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: slow rehearsal of the exact variant and chosen recovery foot
safe lane/run-out and clear stop signal
session upper-body, acceleration, impact, and technical-fatigue budgets fit
excludeOrEscalate: pain, hand slip, unsafe surface/lane, head or knee contact risk, or communication conflict
new neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or coordination concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal start position, target distance, trial cap, recovery, outcome, readiness threshold, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 121 and the research-authored fully-prone Source 710 boundary; start-contact state is a controlled variant.

anatomy.laterality: chosen lead-foot recovery then alternating sprint contacts; balance lead-side exposure across delivery
